issues.summary: Deploy jobs now wait on the whole reusable workflow (needs: [ci]) instead of only biome and tests-finish. That makes license-headers and env-validation new blockers for staging, autodeploy and release, and the change isn't called out.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: ci.yml:44 and :81 are now `needs: [ci]`; base ci.yml:275/312 had `needs: [biome, tests-finish]`. Autodeploy's own needs are unchanged (ci.yml:128, still docker-publish-staging), so F4 is wrong on that detail, but autodeploy is still blocked transitively. The gate is stricter, not weaker, and the PR says that one `needs` line changed, so the impact is minor.

issues.summary: Updated docs point to staging.yml and production.yml, which don't exist. commits-and-prs.md also says the build/deploy jobs live there, when they are still in ci.yml.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: docs/agents/testing.md:36 and docs/agents/commits-and-prs.md:166 name staging.yml/production.yml, but .github/workflows holds only _ci-node.yml, ci.yml, pull-request.yml and unrelated workflows. The build jobs are at ci.yml:39-136. This is a real documentation mismatch that misleads readers.

issues.summary: The two-line arm64 comment was split during the move. Half of it dangles at the end of _ci-node.yml, and ci.yml lost the explanation that the billing README points readers to.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: _ci-node.yml:277 ends with the fragment `# Production runs on arm64 only, ... We run on an` and no job follows. The base ci.yml:268-269 held the full comment above docker-publish-staging, which is now gone from ci.yml:39. src/modules/billing/README.md:192 still refers readers to ci.yml for the arm64 detail.

issues.summary: No caller sets the new node_version, python_version and ref inputs, so for now they do nothing.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: ci.yml:35-37 and pull-request.yml:28-30 pass only `secrets: inherit`; the defaults at _ci-node.yml:18-29 match the old hardcoded values. The PR describes these inputs as deliberate, since later PRs will use them, and they have no concrete cost today.

issues.summary: If a caller ever sets ref, the license-headers diff (BASE_REF..HEAD) would compare the event's base against a different checked-out commit.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: _ci-node.yml:41 checks out inputs.ref, while BASE_REF at :49-53 comes from github.event (PR base or `before`), and the diff runs against HEAD. A non-default ref would check the wrong range. This is latent only: no caller passes ref today.

issues.summary: The '# Krypton' comments sit next to a parameterized node version.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: _ci-node.yml:82/100/164/234. The default is still 24.11.0 (Krypton) at :21, and no caller overrides it, so the comment is accurate for every actual run.

issues.summary: `secrets: inherit` hands all repository secrets to the reusable, when only SAFE_CONFIG_BASE_URI is needed.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: Before this PR, the same jobs ran inside ci.yml, which already had access to every repo secret; a reusable workflow only exposes the secrets its steps reference (_ci-node.yml:175, :248). Exposure doesn't change. Passing just SAFE_CONFIG_BASE_URI would be tighter hardening, but it isn't a regression.

issues.summary: The commit subject and PR title start the description with a capital letter ('Extract'), against the repo's lowercase-initial convention.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: docs/agents/commits-and-prs.md:13 requires a lowercase-initial description. The PR title `feat(ci): Extract ...` breaks that rule, and since main is squash-merged it becomes the permanent history entry; `git log main` already shows `ci: Extract the quality gate ... (#3472)`.

issues.summary: Claim that the required-check rename should be called out prominently in the PR body.
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: The PR body already says in capitals: 'REQUIRED CHECKS MUST BE RENAMED WHEN THIS MERGES', names each new check, and repeats this in the closing note. It is already prominent.
